paraphrase_sample.sample_coverage_rule: ALL left-out flags sampled (count 12 is small enough to check exhaustively -- an ad-hoc call made during this computation, not a pre-registered threshold in design.md/spec.md/tasks.md)

paraphrase_adjusted_gap_rate.headline_rate_used: 12/12 = 100.0% (conservative: an unconfirmed ambiguous case is kept as a gap, not cleared)

per_dispatch_gap_rate.definition: fraction of CHECKED dispatches with at least one memory left out (conservative: ambiguous counts as left-out)

summary.critical_limitation: The structural check only has a real, checkable denominator of n=2 dispatches (and 12 candidate memories total) out of 28 total dispatch moments / 25 non-fork moments. This is because most "dispatch"-type moments in the sampled corpus are NOT actual subagent launches with a separately-constructed prompt (spec.md defines dispatch as "a subagent launch"), but same-context Skill invocations (recall/please/opsx:apply/writing-skills/claude-api/openspec-sync-specs), raw Bash tool calls, or one Workflow-tool launch the mechanical extractor does not parse -- none of these construct an isolable prompt a memory could be "left out" of. Two further genuine dispatches could not be checked because their PARENT main-session transcript no longer exists on disk. This n=2 rate should NOT be read as a representative measurement of the true handoff gap across all dispatches; it is the honest, fully-checkable subset given the real data.
